stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in how the two projections have been used. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A map projection turns Earth's curved surface into a flat image, and every projection distorts something.
• The Mercator projection, published in 1569, keeps the angles between directions accurate.
• Sailors used it to plot courses at a constant compass bearing.
• The Gall-Peters projection, promoted by Arno Peters in 1973, keeps the relative areas of landmasses accurate.
• Some aid organizations adopted it to show the true size of countries near the equator.
choices: The Mercator projection was published in 1569, whereas the Gall-Peters projection was promoted by Arno Peters in 1973.
Sailors used the Mercator projection to plot constant compass bearings, whereas aid groups used the Gall-Peters projection to show countries' true sizes.
Both the Mercator projection and the Gall-Peters projection turn Earth's curved surface into a flat image, and each one distorts something.
The Gall-Peters projection, promoted in 1973, was adopted by some aid organizations to show the true size of countries near the equator.
explanation: The goal limits you to one attribute: how each projection has been used. Choice B names both projections, gives the use of each (sailors plotting bearings, aid groups showing true sizes), and joins them with 'whereas', so the difference is stated outright.

A.why: You saw two items joined by 'whereas' and stopped checking. This choice contrasts the projections' dates, not their uses, so it compares the wrong attribute.

C.why: You picked a sentence that covers both projections, but it states something they have in common. The goal asked for a difference.

D.why: You picked an accurate statement about one projection's use. With no mention of how the Mercator projection was used, nothing is being contrasted.

stem: The student wants to compare the disadvantages of the two approaches. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2023, health officials in Harlow County tested two ways of delivering flu vaccines to rural residents.
• Mobile clinics reached 4,100 residents.
• However, the clinics cost $38 per dose delivered.
• Pharmacy vouchers cost only $12 per dose.
• However, only 31 percent of the mailed vouchers were ever redeemed.
choices: Harlow County health officials tested mobile clinics and pharmacy vouchers in 2023 as two ways of delivering flu vaccines.
Mobile clinics reached 4,100 rural residents, while pharmacy vouchers cost only $12 for each dose of flu vaccine.
Mobile clinics reached 4,100 rural residents in 2023 but cost health officials $38 for each dose delivered.
Mobile clinics cost $38 for each dose delivered, while only 31 percent of the mailed pharmacy vouchers were ever redeemed.
explanation: The goal is narrowed to disadvantages, and it asks for both approaches. Choice D gives the drawback of each, the clinics' high cost per dose and the vouchers' low redemption rate, and sets them side by side with 'while'.

A.why: You picked a choice because it names both approaches. It only says they were tested and never states a disadvantage of either one.

B.why: You found a contrast between both approaches, but it is on the wrong attribute. Reaching 4,100 residents and a $12 cost are advantages, and the goal asked for disadvantages.

C.why: You found a real disadvantage, but only for the mobile clinics. A comparison needs the vouchers' drawback as well.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the endings of the two versions of the tale. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 1962, folklorist Ines Varga recorded two versions of the tale “The Salt Bride.”
• In the coastal village of Mereni, the tale is told by fishermen's families.
• In the Mereni version, the bride returns to the sea and is never seen again.
• In the inland village of Dobra, the tale is told mostly at weddings.
• In the Dobra version, the bride stays, and her husband becomes the richest man in the valley.
choices: In the Mereni version of “The Salt Bride,” the bride returns to the sea forever, whereas in the Dobra version she stays with her husband.
The Mereni version of “The Salt Bride” is told by fishermen's families, whereas the Dobra version is told mostly at weddings.
Ines Varga recorded two versions of “The Salt Bride” in 1962, one in Mereni and one in the inland village of Dobra.
In the Dobra version of “The Salt Bride,” which is told mostly at weddings, the bride's husband becomes the valley's richest man.
explanation: The goal names the attribute: the endings. Choice A gives the ending of each version (the bride leaves forever in Mereni, she stays in Dobra) and links them with 'whereas', which states the difference directly.

B.why: You saw a clean 'whereas' contrast between the two versions, but it contrasts who tells the tale and when. It says nothing about how the tale ends.

C.why: You picked a choice because it mentions both versions. It only says where they were recorded and never states how they differ.

D.why: You picked an accurate description of one ending. Without the Mereni ending, there is nothing to set it against.

stem: The student wants to emphasize how the main spans of the two bridges compare in length. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Carrow Bridge is a suspension bridge completed in 1998.
• Its main span, the distance between its two towers, is 1,240 meters.
• The Tessel Viaduct is a cable-stayed bridge completed in 2011.
• Its main span is 610 meters.
• Cable-stayed designs are generally cheaper to build than suspension designs for spans under 1,000 meters.
choices: The Carrow Bridge was completed in 1998, thirteen years before the cable-stayed Tessel Viaduct was completed in 2011.
The Tessel Viaduct, a cable-stayed bridge completed in 2011, has a main span that measures 610 meters between towers.
The Carrow Bridge's main span of 1,240 meters is roughly twice as long as the Tessel Viaduct's main span of 610 meters.
The Carrow Bridge is a suspension bridge, and the Tessel Viaduct is a cable-stayed bridge with a 610-meter main span.
explanation: The goal asks how the two main spans compare. Choice C gives both lengths and names the relationship with a comparative, 'roughly twice as long' (1,240 is about 2 × 610), so the reader does not have to work it out.

A.why: You found a comparison between the two bridges, but it compares completion dates. The goal asked about span length.

B.why: You picked a choice that gives a span length, but only one. A comparison needs the Carrow Bridge's span too.

D.why: You picked a choice that names both bridges, but it just lists their types side by side. It gives only one span and never says how the two spans relate.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in the likely composition of the two planets. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Astronomers studied two planets orbiting the red dwarf star Kepra-4.
• Kepra-4b completes an orbit every 3 days.
• Its high density suggests a rocky, iron-rich interior.
• Kepra-4c completes an orbit every 41 days.
• Its low density suggests a thick envelope of hydrogen gas.
choices: Kepra-4b completes an orbit every 3 days, whereas Kepra-4c takes 41 days to complete a single orbit of its star.
Kepra-4b appears to have a rocky, iron-rich interior, whereas Kepra-4c appears to have a thick envelope of hydrogen gas.
Kepra-4b appears to have a thick envelope of hydrogen gas, whereas Kepra-4c appears to have a rocky, iron-rich interior.
Kepra-4b and Kepra-4c are two planets that astronomers have studied in orbit around the red dwarf star Kepra-4.
explanation: The goal limits you to composition. Choice B gives each planet's likely makeup as the notes describe it (rocky and iron-rich for Kepra-4b, hydrogen-wrapped for Kepra-4c) and contrasts them with 'whereas'.

A.why: You found a contrast between both planets, but it is about orbital period. The goal asked about composition.

C.why: You recognised the right attribute but did not check which planet goes with which trait. This choice swaps them: the notes tie the rocky interior to Kepra-4b and the hydrogen envelope to Kepra-4c.

D.why: You picked a choice because it names both planets. It never says what either is made of, so it shows no difference.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the difference in how much the two groups improved. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Researchers at a university lab trained 40 amateur runners for eight weeks.
• Half followed an interval program, and the other half ran at a steady, moderate pace.
• Both groups trained for the same total number of hours each week.
• The interval group cut its average 5-kilometer time by 94 seconds.
• The steady-pace group cut its average 5-kilometer time by 41 seconds.
choices: The interval group cut its average 5-kilometer time by 94 seconds, more than twice the steady-pace group's 41-second improvement.
Both groups of amateur runners trained for the same total number of hours each week during the eight-week study.
Interval training makes any runner improve more than twice as much as steady-pace training, as this eight-week study proved.
Over eight weeks of training, the runners who followed the steady-pace program cut their 5-kilometer times by 41 seconds.
explanation: The goal asks how the groups' improvements differed. Choice A gives both improvements and states the relationship, 'more than twice' (94 is more than 2 × 41 = 82), so the size of the gap is spelled out.

B.why: You picked a detail that covers both groups, but it is something they share, equal training hours. The goal asked for a difference.

C.why: You picked the right comparison but let it grow too far. One study of 40 amateurs cannot show what happens to 'any runner', and it did not 'prove' a general rule.

D.why: You picked an accurate result for one group only. Without the interval group's 94 seconds, there is no difference to point to.

stem: The student wants to contrast the effects of the two cities' approaches on restaurant workers' hours. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Economists compared two cities that began raising their minimum wages in 2019.
• Tarrow raised its minimum wage by 15 percent in a single step.
• There, average weekly hours for restaurant workers fell by 2.1 hours.
• Linden phased in the same 15 percent increase over three years.
• There, average weekly hours for restaurant workers were essentially unchanged.
choices: Tarrow raised its minimum wage by 15 percent in a single step, whereas Linden phased in the same increase over three years.
Both Tarrow and Linden raised their minimum wages by 15 percent, and economists compared the two cities' results.
Linden's experience proves that phasing in a minimum wage increase always protects the weekly hours of restaurant workers.
After Tarrow's one-step increase, restaurant workers' weekly hours fell by 2.1, whereas they held steady after Linden's phased increase.
explanation: The goal is narrowed to effects on hours. Choice D gives the outcome in each city (a 2.1-hour drop in Tarrow, no real change in Linden), ties each outcome to that city's approach, and marks the contrast with 'whereas'.

A.why: You found a 'whereas' contrast between the cities, but it contrasts how they raised wages, not what happened to hours. The goal asked about effects.

B.why: You picked a choice that names both cities, but it states what they have in common and gives no result for either.

C.why: You picked up on the right result but accepted too strong a claim. One city's experience cannot show that phasing in 'always' protects hours, and this choice drops Tarrow, so there is no contrast.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in how the two goby species find shelter. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Marine biologist Rafael Oyelaran studied two closely related goby species in a Philippine reef system.
• The ember goby lives at depths of 2 to 15 meters.
• It shares burrows with snapping shrimp.
• The pale goby lives at depths of 40 to 90 meters.
• It shelters alone in crevices of dead coral.
choices: The ember goby lives at depths of 2 to 15 meters, whereas the pale goby lives at depths of 40 to 90 meters.
Rafael Oyelaran studied the ember goby and the pale goby, two closely related species in a Philippine reef system.
The ember goby shares burrows with snapping shrimp, whereas the pale goby shelters alone in the crevices of dead coral.
The ember goby shares burrows with snapping shrimp; similarly, the pale goby shelters alone in the crevices of dead coral.
explanation: The goal limits you to shelter. Choice C gives each species' way of sheltering (sharing shrimp burrows versus hiding alone in dead coral) and uses 'whereas' to mark the two as different.

A.why: You found a clean contrast between both species, but it is about depth. The goal asked how they find shelter.

B.why: You picked a choice because it names both species. It only says they were studied and never states how their shelters differ.

D.why: You matched the right facts but missed the relation word. 'Similarly' presents the two habits as alike, yet shared burrows and solitary crevices are opposites. The sentence hides the difference it should emphasize.
